name: Mauryan rock edicts at Mansehra
description: Fourteen royal proclamations were inscribed in Kharosthi on rocks near a route through the northwestern Mauryan realm.

date.label: mid-third century BCE, approximately
date.basis: The museum or heritage description provides an approximate period, not an exact year.

events.statement: The Mansehra inscriptions present fourteen edicts associated with Ashoka.

evidence.supports: The submitting state’s tentative-list description dates the Mansehra rock inscriptions to the middle of the third century BCE and reports fourteen edicts in Kharosthi beside an ancient route.

events.scope: The date is the state party’s approximate attribution of the inscriptions, not an exact year or proof that all passers-by could read them.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest event established in the sources collected here; not a claim of global priority.

caveats: The Pakistan heritage nomination supplies the date and interpretation. The inscriptions are a particular surviving witness, not the beginning of royal law, communication or writing; placement by a route does not establish literacy or actual readership.

research.note: Independent reader checked the dated event, stated scope and event-specific contributions against the cited passages; other facets retain their stated basis.
